e: DataSync securely moves the existing data to S3 with encryption in transit and integrity checks, and CloudTrail data events record object-level access (reads and writes), which satisfies the audit access at all levels. Management events only cover bucket-level API calls, not object access.

Elastic Beanstalk natively supports Java on Tomcat, and a load-balanced environment (with Auto Scaling) across AZs with a rolling deployment policy keeps the application highly available during updates. Lambda isn't a Tomcat host, and ElastiCache isn't a MySQL replacement.

Give the Lambda function an execution role that Lambda is trusted to assume, with a policy allowing read/write on the DynamoDB table. This avoids long-term access keys entirely. Storing keys in environment variables or Parameter Store is less secure, and the role's trusted service must be Lambda, not DynamoDB.

The first statement allows all EC2 actions only in us-east-1 (ec2:Region condition). The second statement denies StopInstances and TerminateInstances when MFA is not present (BoolIfExists false). Together, members can stop or terminate instances only with MFA, and perform other EC2 actions in us-east-1 only; nothing is allowed in other Regions.

A Lambda function triggered by each .csv upload converts the file to an image immediately and cheaply, with no servers. A lifecycle rule moves the .csv files to Glacier after 1 day, since ML training and audits are planned weeks ahead (so retrieval delays are fine), and expires the images after 30 days. One Zone-IA or RRS are less cost-effective or deprecated, and an hourly Spot job isn't as soon as possible.

ElastiCache for Redis has sorted sets, which compute a top-10 leaderboard in near real time, and it supports persistence (snapshots/AOF) so scores survive a stop and restore. Memcached has no persistence or sorted sets, and CloudFront or read replicas don't compute rankings in real time.

SageMaker is the managed service for building and training ML models, and QuickSight integrates with SageMaker output to visualize the data in BI dashboards, with low operational overhead. Glue ML transforms, Marketplace AMIs, and QuickSight calculated fields aren't suitable for full model training.

A service control policy can deny tag modification actions (such as tag/untag operations on cost allocation tags) except for authorized principals across the organization's accounts, preventing the change. Config rules, CloudTrail, and CloudWatch Logs only detect or log, not prevent.

Pre-provisioning a warm Auto Scaling group and load balancer in the DR Region, a DynamoDB global table that keeps data replicated, and Route 53 DNS failover gives minimal downtime. Launching infrastructure with CloudFormation during a disaster takes longer, and a Lambda-updated record is more complex than native DNS failover.

A Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device moves the 20 TB initial load within the 2-week window, and DMS continues replicating ongoing changes to keep downtime minimal, at a moderate cost. Snowmobile is for exabyte-scale, and a dedicated 1 Gbps Direct Connect takes time to provision and costs more.

Reserved DB instances discount the steady workload, and making the existing DB instance larger (scaling up) accommodates more load without adding infrastructure. Multi-AZ doesn't add read/write capacity, adding another instance adds infrastructure, and on-demand costs more.

AWS WAF attached to the ALB with a rate-based rule blocks IP addresses that exceed a request threshold, even as IPs change, with little impact on legitimate users. Inspector and GuardDuty don't block traffic, and network ACLs can't keep up with changing IPs.

An encrypted snapshot shared with the auditor's account, along with permission to use the KMS key, lets the auditor copy and restore their own database privately without exposing data over the internet or sharing credentials. Read replicas, exports, or shared IAM keys are less secure.

A VPC can have additional (secondary) IPv4 CIDR blocks associated, so adding a CIDR and new subnets increases the available IP addresses in the same VPC with minimal effort. A second VPC with peering, transit gateway, or VPN adds routing and operational work.

Aurora MySQL can restore directly from an RDS for MySQL snapshot (snapshot import), and it can also load a logical dump (mysqldump) that has been uploaded to S3. Snapshots can't be imported via S3 or DMS in that manner, and DMS doesn't import dump files that way.

Static content is driving the scale-out, so serving it from S3 through CloudFront offloads requests from the EC2 instances and cuts the number of On-Demand instances needed, which is the most cost-effective redesign. Reserved or Spot Instances don't reduce the load, and Lambda hosting adds cost.

Lake Formation tag-based access control (LF-TBAC) lets you tag data and grant cross-account permissions by tag, scaling across petabytes and multiple accounts without copying data or managing per-resource grants. Copying data, per-account grants, or Data Exchange involve more effort.

S3 with Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads and downloads of large (gigabyte-sized) files for geographically dispersed users using CloudFront edge locations, cost-effectively and without servers. CacheControl headers don't speed uploads, and EC2 with CloudFront or ElastiCache costs more and doesn't help uploads as much.

Multi-AZ with deletion protection protects the database from failure and accidental deletion, and placing the EC2 instances behind an ALB in an Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs removes the single-AZ and manual provisioning risks. Spot Instances or a single instance reduce reliability.

DataSync can transfer 700 TB over the 10 Gbps Direct Connect link within 90 days while the NAS stays online and usable, with built-in scheduling, integrity checks, and incremental sync of changes. Snowball and tapes are offline and disruptive, and rsync lacks DataSync's performance and management.

S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a 7-year retention period enforces immutable retention, and S3 Batch Operations can apply retention to all existing objects at scale without recopying them. Governance mode can be overridden, and recopying objects takes more effort.

Route 53 health checks with active-active (for example, latency or weighted) routing to the API Gateway endpoints in each Region provide Regional failover for the stateless application. Transit gateways don't route to API Gateway, ALBs can't front Regional API endpoints that way, and CloudFront health checks don't route across Region origins as described.

The Management VPC reaches the data center through VPNs to a single customer gateway device, which is the single point of failure. Adding a second set of VPNs from a second customer gateway device removes it. Peering connections are already redundant by design, and a VPC can have only one virtual private gateway.

RDS Custom for Oracle is a managed service that still allows privileged OS and database access, so third-party features can be supported while AWS handles backups and maintenance, which minimizes effort and cost. RDS for Oracle doesn't permit privileged access, EC2 requires self-management, and rewriting for PostgreSQL isn't quick.

A multi-AZ VPC with separate web, application, and database tiers in private subnets with Auto Scaling for the web and app tiers gives resiliency and scalability. Load balancers in front of the web tier with chained security group references control access, and an RDS Multi-AZ cluster in private subnets accessible only from the application tier gives a resilient, secure database. Single databases or single-instance architectures aren't resilient.
